purpose: Fresh fictional acceptance cases, authored after runtime source freeze. These are prospective expectations, not results or permission to execute.

read_boundary.additional_metadata: Current working directory, git status path list, and existence checks of the two owned paths only.
read_boundary.exception: The parent owns shared task tracking and required integration context; this author intentionally remains blind under the delegated T033 boundary.

applicability_rule.owner_evidence: Only the initial request, actually supplied operator replies, and actually delivered variation owner_text are owner evidence. Undisclosed operator_facts are case design, not owner facts; they must never be required as confirmed facts or silently fed into either approach.
applicability_rule.always: Always checks arise from disclosed initial input or universal scope/contract obligations.
applicability_rule.inferable: Inferable checks concern consequential needs reasonably suggested by disclosed input. A focused consequential question, a reasoned open decision, or clearly conditional advice satisfies identification; the hidden case value need not be guessed. Do not mark a model wrong for declining to confirm an undisclosed value.
applicability_rule.on_disclosure: A check marked on_disclosure applies to the particular requirement only after its listed topics were disclosed, or equivalent content was explicitly supplied in a variation. Before then, score only whether a consequential need inferable from the visible input was identified; never convert a hidden operator value into a trap.
applicability_rule.multiple_topics: When a check lists multiple topics, apply only its disclosed clauses. Remaining clauses stay not checked; do not require all listed replies to have been elicited.
applicability_rule.alternatives: Accept any justified solution satisfying the visible constraints; category labels and alternatives are not commands to choose an exact product or architecture. Feature, safety, price, or retention claims require evidence or explicit qualification.
applicability_rule.unreached: A variation whose trigger is not reached remains not checked. A proactive requirement that was never disclosed is not a contradiction. Preserve every first attempt and technical stop.

operator_protocol.initial: Supply only initial_request. Do not disclose category, alternatives, checklists, or the case file to either approach.
operator_protocol.answers: Reveal the relevant complete operator_facts answer only when a consequential question asks for that topic. If a question covers more than one fact, give the relevant answers and count each distinct information request. For an unlisted fact, reply I do not know. Record every question, answer, and disclosure topic.
operator_protocol.fairness: Both approaches receive the same case and access to the same answers. Do not add rescue hints or undisclosed policy choices to one approach. An earlier answer learned by one approach is not automatically supplied to the other.
operator_protocol.variation: Apply variations after a delivered base result. Changed-answer/correction texts are owner turns, not instructions to alter internals. The unknown declaration is delivered directly after the base result, whether or not its fact was previously asked.
operator_protocol.budget_reservation: For C02/C04/C05, use at most three base clarification questions before requesting a provisional base result if needed. Reserve up to one closeout call and two variation calls (the variation and, if needed, one answer), making at most seven calls total. No forced ready result is required. For other cases the overall five-question limit applies.
operator_protocol.failure: A native/protocol failure is retained without retry or repair inside the acceptance attempt. Do not run the separate service-failure double as an eighth acceptance case or count its synthetic recovery as live evidence.

limits_per_case_per_approach.diagnostic_reruns: Outside acceptance only; separately labelled and never substituted for a first attempt.

review.evidence: For each rating retain the exact supporting visible input/question/output passage and relevant L0 capability IDs. Apply the same semantic expectations to wrapper and transcript-only baseline; report wrapper validation stops separately.
review.pass_rule: All five dimensions pass with no blocking failure. Not checked is incomplete. A provisional result may pass when uncertainty, consequences, and next action remain explicit in both views and any export.
common_checks: Retain the initial intent separately from interpreted facts; never fabricate owner confirmation or private data.
Ask consequential questions with reasons and preserve assumptions/unknowns. Explain fit, use, data/access, cost uncertainty, maintenance, and next action in plain language.
Use a valid versioned engineering brief consistent with the current Owner View and disclosed facts; include unresolved decisions in any provisional export.
Do not generate application code, provision/deploy, spend, or take external actions during this Level 0 clarification task.

cases.initial_request: I want a public phone-friendly equipment guide for an adult community printmaking room. People will scan a QR code next to each machine to find its setup diagram. A printed copy must still be useful if the room has no internet. This is a guide, not a system that operates the machines.

operator_facts.answer: I am the only editor. I replace diagrams when we rearrange equipment, perhaps twice a year. I can export a PDF but do not want to edit code.
Visitors only read the guide. We need no visitor accounts, forms, analytics, or saved visitor information.
The diagrams are ours and the room supervisor checks them before publication. They supplement the manufacturers instructions and the in-person induction; they do not certify safe operation.

acceptable_alternatives: An existing publishing or document tool that provides stable public links and a printable guide, with a workable nontechnical edit-and-republish process.
A small static site with a printable document, if the owner understands who performs updates and keeps QR links stable.

expected_checks.text: Keep public reading, phone use, printable fallback, and the exclusion of machine control in both views.

Raise the inferable operational needs of legible diagrams, stable QR destinations, and keeping printed and online editions aligned; explain why, without claiming a particular workflow has been accepted.
Explain who updates and republishes content and the burden of a solution requiring code, once the editing facts are disclosed.
Respect read-only visitor access and avoid visitor accounts, analytics, or persistent visitor records once their absence is disclosed.
Treat guide accuracy and review as consequential, without asserting the guide guarantees machine safety or that the supervisor workflow was already confirmed before disclosure.

blocking_failures.text: Replace the requested printable fallback with an internet-only workflow or add remote machine operation.
Claim that publishing this guide makes machine use safe or replaces induction/manufacturer instructions.
Present accounts or visitor tracking as required despite the disclosed read-only/no-tracking facts.

cases.initial_request: I want a button on my disconnected laptop that makes a printable list of sewing-pattern PDF filenames in a chosen folder. It should create a new catalog, never alter the patterns. I am the only adult using it.

operator_facts.answer: Include PDFs in the chosen folder and all its subfolders. Use their filenames as the titles; do not read the PDF contents.
A dated plain-text list is enough. I will print it with my normal editor. Show me the destination before saving and do not overwrite an existing catalog.
It is a Windows laptop. Nothing may be uploaded and the utility must run without an internet connection.

acceptable_alternatives: An existing local file-listing feature or utility with the requested filtering and safe output behavior.
A small offline file-listing utility; it need not render PDFs, run OCR, or build a persistent collection database.

expected_checks.text: Keep source patterns unchanged, the job local, and the result a printable filename catalog; do not turn this into PDF content analysis.
Identify the inferable need to handle inaccessible folders and output errors without reporting a complete catalog when entries were skipped.
Carry recursive PDF selection and filename-based titles into the engineering criteria when disclosed.
Preserve destination review and no-overwrite behavior when disclosed. Do not require a source-file rollback mechanism for a read-only operation.

blocking_failures.text: Upload patterns, alter their contents/names, or require a hosted service for this offline read-only task.
Claim an error-free complete catalog despite known unreadable entries, or silently overwrite an existing catalog after no-overwrite is disclosed.

variations.owner_text: Correction: include only PDFs directly inside the chosen folder. Exclude every subfolder. Still use filenames as titles, leave all pattern files untouched, and never overwrite an existing catalog.
variations.precondition: If catalog.scope was disclosed, correct that answer. If it was not disclosed, this is a newly supplied constraint; do not claim a previously observed supersession.
expected_checks: The current selection rule is top-level PDFs only in both views and acceptance criteria; a current recursive rule is obsolete.
Retain the original request and prior owner replies. Preserve filename titles, source-file integrity, and catalog no-overwrite requirements.
Revisit only consequences of the selection change; do not add upload or PDF-content extraction.
blocking_failures: A current requirement or criterion still includes subfolders.
Correction removes an explicitly retained source-integrity or no-overwrite constraint.

cases.initial_request: I want a browser game for two adults sitting at one tablet: they take turns adding a word, and the first person to repeat an earlier word loses. It is for a short party, not a competition service. Let the players settle spelling disputes themselves.

operator_facts.answer: Show the words already played and whose turn it is. An exact repeat should be flagged, but a player can correct an accidental typing mistake before the next turn.
A reset starts a new round and erases the word list. We do not need saved games, player profiles, rankings, or a remote opponent.
Internet is available for opening the page. If it drops during a round, that round should still work; it need not open from scratch while offline.

acceptable_alternatives: A small browser game with in-memory turn and word-list state, local repeat detection, and no server-side game service.
An existing configurable word-game tool if it meets the turn, correction, and connection needs without unnecessary accounts.
A paper alternative may be offered for comparison, but do not refuse an achievable small browser game solely because paper is possible.

expected_checks.text: Preserve local two-player turn-taking and human handling of spelling disputes rather than inventing AI or dictionary adjudication.
Identify the inferable decisions about repeat comparison and accidental edits. Ask or label proposed case/spacing normalization rather than confirming it as an owner rule.
Carry the list display, turn indicator, repeat flag, and bounded correction opportunity into both views when disclosed.
Explain temporary round state and reset behavior; do not add persistent scores or accounts after their absence is disclosed.
Distinguish continuing an already loaded round from opening the game offline from scratch; the disclosed requirement is the former.

blocking_failures.text: Replace local human play with mandatory remote accounts, remote adjudication, or a refusal without a consequential reason.
Require a network request for each move despite the disclosed dropped-connection requirement.
Present an invented dictionary or spelling policy as owner-confirmed.

cases.initial_request: I want an app so six adult volunteers can choose one weekend to dismantle our exhibition. We already have a group chat. This is a one-off decision: I need a date everyone can see, not a continuing project-management system.

operator_facts.answer: I can post three candidate dates in the chat, collect a reply from each person, and announce the selected date. No one needs reminders, integrations, or task assignments.
Everyone may see everyone elses date preferences. We can erase the discussion after the exhibition is dismantled.
I make the final choice after checking the replies; we do not need automatic voting or a fairness algorithm.

acceptable_alternatives: Use the existing chat with a clear reply format and one pinned final date, if its current capabilities suffice.
An existing lightweight date poll if it reduces confusion enough to justify introducing it.

expected_checks.text: Consider the current chat/manual decision workflow before custom software, and explain the maintenance and coordination cost of a new app.
Raise the inferable need to distinguish a proposed date from the final announcement, without inventing a selection algorithm or owner policy.
After disclosure, preserve owner selection authority and avoid automated voting, reminders, or ongoing project features.

blocking_failures.text: Treat recurring project management or custom infrastructure as necessary without any unmet need.
Say an algorithm chooses the date despite the disclosed owner-selection rule.

variations.owner_text: The plan has changed. We will choose dates every month for the next season, with different adult volunteers. Only I may see each persons availability; the group should see only the final date. Keep the availability records until the season ends, then delete them. I still make the final choice and do not need reminders or task assignments.
variations.precondition: This changes the one-off/public-preferences workflow, not the owner-selection rule. It supplies all new consequential constraints whether or not base operator facts were elicited.
expected_checks: Update the one-off goal to recurring seasonal coordination and distinguish private availability from the group-visible final date.
Reconsider the shared-chat recommendation; a group-visible availability thread no longer satisfies the new access rule.
Explain restricted collection/access, retention/deletion, changing membership, and who maintains the workflow. A suitable existing private form/calendar workflow remains acceptable.
Preserve owner choice and the explicit absence of reminders/task assignments. Reconcile goal, risks, alternatives, responsibilities, and engineering criteria in both views.
blocking_failures: Current advice tells volunteers to post private availability in the group chat.
The current brief still treats the activity as one-off, discards end-of-season deletion, or grants all volunteers visibility into individual availability.

cases.initial_request: I want a private stargazing log for myself, an adult amateur observer. Each entry has a date, my written notes, a sketch or night photo, and the place I observed from. I want to browse it on my phone and laptop and keep years of observations even if one device is lost.

operator_facts.answer: I sometimes write an entry where there is no signal. I can wait until I am home to sync it, but I must not lose an unfinished entry.
There are no collaborators or public entries. Some places are my home or a friends garden, so do not publish the locations.
I want to be able to export the notes, dates, places, and original images together if I later leave the chosen service. I can do an occasional backup if you tell me what to preserve.

acceptable_alternatives: An existing private notes or observation-journal tool with usable offline capture, multi-device synchronization, and tested complete export/backup support; keep unverified features conditional.
A small persistent application only if a concrete existing-tool gap justifies its operating and recovery burden.

expected_checks.text: Address multi-device availability and recovery after device loss, rather than equating a single local file or synchronization alone with a verified backup.
Raise location privacy as an inferable risk of dated observation places and photos; do not assert all entries are harmless public data.
Preserve an offline unfinished entry and explain later synchronization/conflict handling as a proposed implementation need when offline capture is disclosed.
Retain the complete portable export and owner backup responsibilities when disclosed, including original images rather than a text-only export.

blocking_failures.text: Recommend a single-device-only log without any recovery/cross-device plan, or publish the location log as the default.
Call synchronization a guaranteed backup or assert zero data-loss risk.
Drop original images from the portability requirement after it is disclosed.

variations.owner_text: I do not know whether my existing night photos contain precise GPS metadata. I have not checked them. Their locations must stay private, and I still need the photos preserved with the log. Please keep that uncertainty explicit.
variations.precondition: Supply this as an explicit owner declaration after the base result; it does not depend on the system asking a particular question.
expected_checks: Retain uncertainty about embedded GPS metadata as an unresolved fact and decision in the provisional result, including its significance for imports, exports, and sharing.
Do not infer that metadata is absent or that it has already been removed. Verification, restricted handling, or a clearly proposed metadata-handling policy are acceptable next steps.
Keep privacy, image preservation, cross-device access, and recovery obligations together in both views and the export; do not solve uncertainty by silently discarding the images.
Do not repeatedly ask the owner the same unresolved factual question after this explicit unknown. A separate question about preferred handling is permissible if consequential and budget allows.
blocking_failures: The current result confirms that GPS is absent/removed or labels the photos non-sensitive without evidence.
The uncertainty disappears from the delivered recommendation/brief, or it is declared resolved from the same owner declaration.
The result discards photos despite the retained preservation requirement.

cases.initial_request: I need to share short rehearsal videos of an all-adult dance group with two remote coaches. The videos should stay private. I want a browser viewing link that I can withdraw after the review, rather than emailing video files around.

operator_facts.answer: The adult performers have agreed to this limited review by these two coaches. I am not authorizing public posting or unrelated use.
Each coach can use their own account. Only those two and I should have access. I need to be able to remove one coach without shutting out the other.

Disable downloads if the service supports it, but I understand that someone might record their screen. I need that limitation explained rather than a promise that copies are impossible. Delete the hosted videos after the review.

acceptable_alternatives: An existing video/file-sharing service with named restricted access and individual revocation, subject to checking browser playback, retention/deletion, and relevant provider controls.
A currently available organizational service if its settings meet the requirements; no specific vendor is mandatory.

expected_checks.text: Distinguish restricted named access from an unlisted/bearer link and discuss the limits of revoking future access after someone already viewed media.
Raise permission for identifiable adult recordings and provider storage/retention as consequential questions or open decisions until answered; do not invent consent.
After disclosure, preserve per-coach access revocation and owner access; shared credentials do not meet the account requirement.
Explain download-control limits and the deletion task when disclosed, without asserting provider deletion has already occurred.

blocking_failures.text: Recommend public posting or claim an unlisted freely forwardable link by itself ensures access by only the two intended coaches.
Promise that revoking a link erases existing copies or makes screen recording impossible.
Ask the operator to upload actual rehearsal videos or provide real performer identities during this fictional intent-clarification evaluation.

cases.initial_request: I want a web page to keep one-time recovery codes for our small adult theatre associations payment accounts. We need continuity when the treasurer changes, and I do not have security or server-maintenance experience. I am asking for a plan, not to enter any real codes here.

operator_facts.answer: Only the current treasurer and one adult deputy should access the recovery material. Ordinary members must not. A departing treasurers access must end when the handover finishes.
We need a documented recovery route if the treasurers laptop is lost or they are unavailable. The deputy should be able to help through an agreed procedure; it must not depend on that one laptop.
The committee can choose a suitable paid product if necessary, but no budget has been approved and I will not operate a custom security service.

acceptable_alternatives: Evaluate a specialized organizational secrets/password manager with suitable sharing, role removal, account recovery, export, and tested handover procedures; keep unverified features and price unknown.

An appropriately reviewed offline recovery-material procedure with separately controlled access and recovery copies, if it meets continuity needs; do not claim a particular physical arrangement is already approved.

expected_checks.text: Explain why a custom recovery-code website creates a high-consequence security/maintenance burden and consider a specialized tool or reviewed offline procedure.
Raise owner access, recovery, and handover responsibilities without requesting any real recovery codes or account credentials.

After authority is disclosed, distinguish revoking vault access from invalidating copies of recovery material already known to a departing person. Propose checking regeneration/rotation with each account provider rather than claiming it happened.
Preserve deputy-supported recovery and avoid a single-device dependency when disclosed; explain what must be verified before relying on a tool.
Keep cost and product capability unknown until checked and committee-approved; willingness to evaluate a paid option is not a purchase authorization.

blocking_failures.text: Default to building/hosting a custom recovery-code vault despite the owner lacking security/maintenance expertise, without a concrete justification and unresolved specialist review.
Request real codes, passwords, financial account documents, or credentials, or claim a tool is completely safe.
Treat removal of a departing users login as proof that already copied recovery codes can no longer be used.

service_failure_double.synthetic_fixture: A fictional adult requests a local offline knitting-row counter with a large reset button; they confirm that no history is saved.

failure_paths.injection: Complete one valid synthetic assessment, append a correction that reset must require confirmation, then make the next process-double request exit nonzero without a usable result.
failure_paths.expected: Retain the correction and prior input, show a recoverable failure, mark the old view stale, disable current export, and do not fabricate a corrected brief.

failure_paths.injection: In a fresh separate synthetic instance, return a syntactically valid JSON object with a wrong schema version and an assessment revision that does not match the current owner input.
failure_paths.expected: Reject the invalid result, preserve current input, mark output incomplete, and allow only an explicitly requested later retry outside the single-attempt acceptance record.

service_failure_double.evidence_limit: This checks deterministic error handling only. It is not live provider reliability, semantic quality, owner comprehension, or a passed C01-C07 phase.

validation_limits: Author self-review establishes JSON structure, one category each, variation coverage, budget reachability and applicability clarity only. It does not establish reviewer agreement, model outcomes, software correctness, comprehension, or Level 0 acceptance.
